title: Multiplication of 2-Digit by 2-Digit Numbers
seo_title: Grade 4 Multiplication Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Multiply at least whole 2-digit by 2-digit numbers.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 4 multiplication worksheets: grid method, 2-digit and 3-digit by 1-digit, 2-digit by 2-digit and word problems. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Break into tens and units, multiply, then add.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Break the numbers into tens and units: 34 × 26 = 30 × 26 + 4 × 26.
  • In the grid method, multiply each part and add: 600 + 180 + 80 + 24 = 884.
  • In columns, multiply by the units first, then by the tens (write a 0 first), then add.
  • Estimate first: 34 × 26 is about 30 × 30 = 900.

Examples

Example

43 × 25

40 × 25 = 1 000

3 × 25 = 75

Answer: 1 075

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Missing the 0When you multiply by 2 tens, the answer is in tens.
Forgetting to carryAdd the carried digit.
Only the unitsMultiply every part.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 4 say about multiplication?
faq.a: Multiply at least whole 2-digit by 2-digit numbers, using properties of operations and techniques such as the grid method, doubling and halving, and breaking down numbers.
Splitting both numbers into parts in a grid and adding the products.

Which partial products add up to 87 × 74?
items.e: Each part of one number multiplies each part of the other, so there are 4 partial products. Break apart 87 = 80 + 7 and 74 = 70 + 4. 80 × 70 = 5 600, 80 × 4 = 320, 7 × 70 = 490, 7 × 4 = 28. Add: 5 600 + 320 + 490 + 28 = 6 438.

Which partial products add up to 16 × 53?

items.q: Which partial products add up to 94 × 42?

items.q: Each crate on a lorry has a mass of 136 kg. The lorry carries 7 crates. What is their total mass?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 7 × 136 kg. Ones: 6 × 7 = 42. Write 2, exchange 4 tens. Tens: 3 × 7 + 4 = 25. Write 5, exchange 2 hundreds. Hundreds: 1 × 7 + 2 = 9. Write 9. Answer: 952. So the answer is 952 kg.

items.q: There are 28 children in each class. The juniors have 7 classes. How many junior children are there?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 7 × 28 children. Ones: 8 × 7 = 56. Write 6, exchange 5 tens. Tens: 2 × 7 + 5 = 19. Write 19. Answer: 196. So the answer is 196 children.

items.q: A train has 6 carriages. Each carriage has 74 seats. How many seats are on the train?
items.e: Equal groups, so multiply: 6 × 74 seats. Ones: 4 × 6 = 24. Write 4, exchange 2 tens. Tens: 7 × 6 + 2 = 44. Write 44. Answer: 444. So the answer is 444 seats.

items.q: A school has 6 boxes of 144 pencils. It gives out 500 pencils. How many pencils are left?
items.e: Step 1: pencils: 6 × 144 = 864 (4 × 6 = 24, write 4, exchange 2; 4 × 6 + 2 = 26, write 6, exchange 2; 1 × 6 + 2 = 8). Step 2: 864 − 500 = 364.
